patent_grounding.rationale: Revision 6 correctly describes the patent-supported three-component housing and outlet, two-half impeller, rotating inlet tube(s), seal, motor drive alternatives, optional flange/bearings, centrifugal action, and weep indication. The supply-to-impeller external boundary is cautiously framed as a boundary interface and its flow note explicitly avoids asserting an unsupported internal housing-to-tube topology. One wording issue remains in the housing description: 'At least one outer component includes an inlet' is supported by Claim 1; it does not imply a specific internal connection.

functional_completeness.rationale: Prior inlet gap is addressed: SUPPLY output now mates to IMPELLER fluid_in, which is expressly the rotating tube intake boundary, and IMPELLER discharge mates to housing volute. The external outlet receiver is connected. The pump action was de-duplicated into drive, outward forcing, transfer into volute, and routing to outlet. Seal-load and leak indication are represented.

flow_consistency.rationale: Fluid boundary and internal discharge flows have compatible hydraulic_fluid types and source/out directions. Supply-to-impeller and impeller-to-volute connections are coherent; housing outlet to receiver is coherent. Rotary motor-to-impeller ports are matching mechanical_rotary out/in. No transformation is modeled as a mismatched interface.

claim_traceability.rationale: R_PUMP and R_SEAL_LOAD are grounded in Claims 1/8. Claim-dependent motor drive and single/dual inlet options are preserved in descriptions/notes rather than asserted as a single universal arrangement. The optional parts and leak indication have patent passage citations.

interfaces.rationale: The external supply interface now connects to the impeller fluid-entry port corresponding to the rotating hollow inlet tube(s), resolving the prior disconnected intake issue without inventing a housing-to-impeller internal connection. Motor drive, discharge-to-volute, and outlet-to-receiver interfaces are compatible and each connection is represented once.

textbook_application.rationale: Separate supply and receiver context components with directed boundary flows apply the textbook context/interface principle. The textbook material informs modeling method only; all asserted pump facts derive from patent passages.

summary: Independently reviewed saved revision 6 against its actual cited patent passages, the prior revision-5 findings, and relevant textbook modeling guidance. The formerly unmodeled inlet path is now represented as an external source boundary directly mating to the impeller's rotating inlet-tube entry port, with notes preserving the one/two-tube variants and explicitly avoiding a guessed internal connection. The repeated outward-forcing step was removed; behavior and flow progression are coherent. Motor drive alternatives remain qualified. No structural, citation-grounding, flow, claim traceability, or interface issues remain. No candidate changes made.
